Incorporating SLOOS evidence, the macro tone of the June 10, 2020 FOMC statement remains negative and is further darkened by the credit-supply channel. The April 2020 SLOOS shows broad-based tightening across banks: standards tightened and spreads widened for C&I loans (including to large and middle‑market firms) with higher costs for credit lines; CRE and multifamily lending standards and terms tightened; HELOC standards tightened; and banks cited the deteriorating economic outlook, reduced risk tolerance, and liquidity needs as key reasons. Demand weakened notably in CRE/multifamily, banks focused on existing clients rather than new ones, and many expected further tightening. While policy backstops (QE in Treasuries/MBS/CMBS, repos, zero rates) improved market functioning, SLOOS indicates that bank intermediation remained restrictive, implying a drag on credit availability that reinforces the downside risks highlighted in the statement. Net: more negative than the FSR-only assessment given the additional constraint from bank lending.
